A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Truncated Consistency Models. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet generation results, training trajectories, design ablations and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds COYO-trained text-to-image results evaluated on MSCOCO, with quantitative scores and generated examples.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds a consistency-distillation adaptation for text-to-image generation with fixed classifier-free guidance, whereas v1's TCM experiments use consistency training. The core two-stage procedure, truncated parameterization, boundary loss and time-sampling design remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds COYO training and MSCOCO evaluation for text-to-image generation. This substantially extends task coverage beyond v1's unconditional CIFAR-10 and class-conditional ImageNet generation by introducing text-conditioned generation.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparison methods. The added text-to-image experiment extends the existing standard Stage 1 versus truncated Stage 2 comparison to another task; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces a distinct experimental protocol: Stable Diffusion 1.5 initialization, guidance scale 6, batch size 512, 80,000 Stage 1 iterations followed by 200,000 Stage 2 iterations, and zero-shot MSCOCO FID using 30,000 generated samples. Existing CIFAR-10/ImageNet settings are retained; their newly explicit training lengths are documentation additions.

E4.justification: Figure 3 revises several Stage 1 and Stage 2 dFID trajectories used to analyze denoising versus generation, including removing the earlier Stage 1 spike at t = 0.8. The sampling-distribution, boundary-weight, dividing-time and training-stage ablations, along with appendix stability analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests for the experimental results. v2 continues reporting individual scores and trajectories; the new 30,000-sample evaluation is not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for a substantially different task: Table 5 reports zero-shot MSCOCO FID of 18.32 for Stage 1 and 15.58 for Stage 2, accompanied by text-to-image examples in Figure 6. Figure 3 also changes plotted training trajectories. Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results; the MSCOCO scores are newly reported results, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and derivations remain unchanged. v1's background and TCM-objective appendices B–C become appendices D–E in v2, retaining the same equations and reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the claims about the denoising–generation trade-off, two-stage truncated training, improved generation quality and training stability. The new appendix experiment broadens supporting evidence without redefining those main claims.

C2.justification: The relocated limitations clarify that the reported 18% training-time overhead is per iteration and specify that the remaining quality gap concerns one-step generation. Appendix B presents the new experiment as scalability evidence while qualifying it as a small-batch validation. Existing capacity-allocation and stability interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F explicitly states training lengths: CIFAR-10 250K/200K iterations, EDM2-S 150K/120K, and EDM2-XL 40K for Stage 2. These are newly documented rather than stated budget revisions. Appendix B supplies text-to-image settings and a COYO access reference; Section 4.3 newly clarifies that most baseline scores come from the original papers.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds positioning against expert denoisers and truncated diffusion methods, citing Balaji et al. and Zheng et al., plus a phased consistency citation to Wang et al. Additional references support the text-to-image setup. These are focused additions rather than a substantial reframing of novelty.

P1.justification: v2 moves limitations from the conclusion to Appendix A, inserts a text-to-image appendix, and renumbers the retained appendices. Local explanatory additions and reference updates accompany this restructuring, while most main-text prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the paired text-to-image display in Figure 6 and the MSCOCO table, redraws Figure 3 with revised axis ranges and legend placement, and relocates retained appendix figures and sample galleries. The overall document design and existing table structures remain stable.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful applicability evidence beyond CIFAR-10/ImageNet and improves transparency about training lengths, baseline provenance and per-iteration overhead. The new text-to-image study remains preliminary: it compares stages with unequal training budgets and reports no uncertainty estimates. These additions support a limited overall improvement while the core method, theory and headline benchmark results remain stable.
